Thanks Jonas — attaching our redlines. A few clarifications up front:

1) Invoicing cadence: Acme prefers quarterly invoicing with monthly usage detail and a final true-up at quarter close. We cannot accept continuous monthly invoices for this engagement.
2) Min commit: We are open to a 12-month minimum but want a ramp provision for months 1–3 capped at 50% of commit credits; if trailing 6-month usage < 60% we want a partial credit back.
3) Net terms: Procurement requests Net 60; finance will push back if Net 30/45 is insisted upon.
4) VAT: For EU customers, Acme will remit VAT where required; however, we need Redwood to provide VAT invoices and confirmation that Redwood is not withholding VAT on our behalf.

I attached: redlines_orderform_acme.docx (track changes) and a draft PO. Please review and advise if you need alternate phrasing for the ramp/credit mechanics.

Team —

I've reviewed Acme's redlines and drafted recommended language. Summary of key positions:

1) Minimum commitment and ramp: propose a 12-month committed term with a 3-month ramp period. During months 1–3, charges will reflect 50% of the monthly committed rate. If the average usage over months 7–12 is less than 60% of the committed quantity, Redwood will apply a one-time credit equal to 25% of the shortfall (calculated as (commit - actual)*monthly rate), capped at 50% of total contract value. This preserves revenue predictability while providing a predictable clawback.

2) Invoicing cadence: Accept quarterly invoices with monthly usage detail and a quarter-end true-up. Finance should confirm the mechanics for proration and revenue recognition.

3) Net terms & credit: recommend offering Net 45 for this enterprise deal (compromise between Net 30 and their Net 60 request). If procurement insists on Net 60, we require an approval from Sales Director and Finance VP with a one-time signing credit to offset cashflow risk.

4) Taxes & VAT: Redwood's position is that taxes (including VAT) are borne by the customer unless Redwood is required by law to collect. Proposed clause: "Customer is responsible for all sales, use, value-added or other taxes arising from Customer's purchase, excluding taxes based on Redwood's net income. If Customer claims tax exemption, it must provide valid exemption certificates in advance."

5) Attachments: I've prepared OF_redlines_LB_v1.docx (tracked) with the exact wording and commentary for negotiation points.

If Ben approves Net 45 and the quarterly invoicing flow, I'll prepare a consolidated redline to send back to Acme with rationale for the 25% cap on credits.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Jordan / procurement team —

Thanks for the patience while we reviewed your requests. Attached is an updated Order Form (orderform_ACME_v3.pdf) and summary of the compromise positions below:

- Invoicing: Redwood accepts quarterly invoicing with monthly usage detail + quarter-end true-up.
- Min commit: 12-month committed term with a 3-month ramp (50% billing during ramp). If average usage months 7–12 < 60% of commit, Redwood will apply a one-time credit equal to 25% of the shortfall, capped at 50% of the total contract value.
- Net terms: Redwood can accept Net 45. If Acme requires Net 60, we'll need executive approval and propose a one-time signing credit (to be documented in the Order Form).
- Taxes/VAT: Proposed tax clause attached — customer is responsible for taxes unless Redwood is legally required to collect. We will provide VAT invoices where applicable. If Acme provides valid exemption documentation in advance, we will not charge VAT.

Ask: Please review the attached final redline and confirm whether we should proceed to DocuSign. I have created a DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.net/Acme-Redwood-OrderForm-2027 — if you can confirm by EOD Friday (8/27) we can lock the pricing and start onboarding.
